# Desktop pressure summary (generated by offline analyzer)

> Label: **daily desktop load, not experimental load**. No training or
> evaluation job was running. Nothing here measures experiment throughput or
> tail latency, and no value is a cleanup benefit. Every source record has
> `cleanup_performed: false`; the tool only did read-only queries.

Source: `logs/desktop-pressure.jsonl` (gitignored raw log), 90 samples, 10 s
apart, `--with-processes` on every sample, run_id
`85b421c280b343b68e29f9275f4bf55a`, 2026-10-18T13:59:33Z .. 14:14:23Z UTC
(21:59:33-22:14:23 Asia/Shanghai, 2026-10-18). Host: 47.1 GiB physical RAM,
commit limit 95.1 GiB, one pagefile with about 13.2-13.4 GiB used at start
and end. Reproduce with:

```powershell
python -m cpu_memory_cleanup --analyze logs\desktop-pressure.jsonl
python -m cpu_memory_cleanup --analyze logs\desktop-pressure.jsonl --json
```

Warnings: 94 total = 4 first-tick rate warnings (no previous PDH interval on
sample 1) + 90 "process ranking is incomplete" (about 4 of ~1000 processes per
sample were protected, access-denied or exited). 0 overruns.

## Compared with the idle baseline (same machine, same day)

| Metric (median) | Idle baseline 20:09-20:24 | Desktop pressure 21:59-22:14 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Available GiB | 27.144 | 8.226 |
| Commit used GiB | 46.463 | 64.699 |
| Standby total GiB | 18.536 | 6.727 |
| Page reads/sec | 26.800 | 8.700 |
| Pages input/sec | 144.500 | 52.501 |

Both are 90 x 10 s windows of about 15 minutes; neither had experimental load.
Available stayed between 6.37 and 9.07 GiB the whole window, and standby
shrank to about 6-8 GiB. Hard-fault medians stayed low, with short bursts
(pages input/sec p95 about 5187, max about 25772), so in this window the host
was under capacity pressure but was not paging continuously. The 12 transitions
of at least 1 GiB were all paired commit up/down swings of about 1.1-1.6 GiB
that reverted within one or two samples; no single large release like the
external one in the idle baseline happened.

## Top working-set owners

Ranking is the per-sample top 10 by working set. For each name the analyzer
keeps only the largest single instance in each sample; same-name instances are
**not** added together, and working set includes shared pages, so none of these
numbers is a reclaimable amount.

| Process | Samples present | Max instances in top 10 | Largest instance median GiB | Largest instance max GiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| codex.exe | 90 | 1 | 1.813 | 1.899 |
| ChatGPT.exe | 90 | 6 | 1.592 | 2.010 |
| T'OWEI.exe | 90 | 1 | 0.585 | 0.591 |
| blender.exe | 10 | 1 | 0.558 | 0.589 |
| 360se.exe | 90 | 4 | 0.542 | 1.056 |

The biggest single process is under 2 GiB, while about 39 GiB of physical
memory is in use and commit is about 64.7 GiB. Top-10 working sets therefore
do not explain where most of the memory is. Hunch to verify next (not a
finding): much of it is spread across many smaller processes, private commit
that is paged out, or kernel / driver / GPU-related allocations that a working
set ranking cannot see. The cross-check in backlog item 2 should look at that
gap before any mitigation is designed.
